cards.front: What should you know about ao6 requirement?
cards.back: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. Spelling errors can cost you marks across all writing questions.

cards.front: What should you know about exceptions to remember?
cards.back: weird, seize, neither, either, foreign, height, their, heir

cards.front: What should you know about english terms?
cards.back: metaphor, simile, personification, alliteration, onomatopoeia, juxtaposition, semantic field, foreshadowing, narrative, perspective

cards.front: What should you know about tip?
cards.back: When in doubt, write the word down. Often your eye will catch an error that your brain misses.

cards.front: What should you know about spelling exam strategy?
cards.back: Spelling accuracy directly affects your AO6 mark (16 marks). Frequent errors can cap you at Level 1 or 2, regardless of how good your content is. Before the exam: Memorise the top 10 commonly misspelt words (accommodation, separate, definitely, necessary, occurrence, beginning, disappear, environment, privilege, embarrass). Learn the mnemonic for each. During writing: If you're unsure how to spell a word, use a simpler alternative you can spell correctly. "Huge" is better than a misspelt "collosal". Accuracy always beats ambition. Proofreading (last 5 minutes): Read through your work specifica
there (e.g. their = belonging to them; there = place)
you're (e.g. your = belonging to you; you're = you are)
it's (e.g. its = belonging to it; it's = it is)
too / two (e.g. to = direction; too = also/excessively; two = number)
wear / were (e.g. where = place; wear = clothing; were = past tense)
off (e.g. of = belonging/relating; off = away from)
effect (e.g. affect = verb (to influence); effect = noun (result))
